IBEW.text:
**Trampin the IBEW Indoor Locals — Saturday, September 5, 2026**

**LU-494 Milwaukee, WI** is moving bodies fast. Sixty hands needed across 42 calls, and the Port Washington Data Center alone is soaking 60 JWs between Gurtz and Cupertino—both offering JW wage plus **$10/hr base wage increase**. Westphal's Oak Creek Power Plant call hits **$60/hr** with **$1,050 per week** subsistence for travelers over 70 miles and a 5% quarterly bonus; that's a 5-10 grind, but the money talks.

**LU-430 Racine, WI** is tighter but sweeter. Eleven calls, 76 hands on book, and Microsoft Mount Pleasant is pulling 53 JWs across four contractors (Gerdes, Pieper, Staff, Kelso Burnett) all at **$62.51/hr**. Long sleeves and safety-t mandatory; start dates already hit (late June/late month). Reciprocal JWs welcome.

**LU-354 Salt Lake City, UT** has 26 calls stacked with **$46.22/hr** work across four contractors. QTS Eagle Mountain (Winward), Facebook Eagle Mountain (Cache Valley), and Nucor's 12-hour day shifts starting September 13th all hit the same rate, plus Nucor running continuous OT. Five-day weeks with Saturday availability on some calls.

**LU-613 Atlanta, GA** remains the steady volume play: 55 calls, 354 hands needed, Inglett & Stubbs and Whitehead moving 80+ JWs on QTS data center work at **$42/hr** across 4-10's and 2-8's (Saturdays operational). Shop work available through Miller Electrical too.

**LU-1547 Anchorage, AK** sits strange: 54 calls, only 66 hands on book means Book 1 is nearly clear. Work ranges telecom-to-inside to tree trimming; Alcan Electric's inside JW call runs **$57.44/hr** with Certificate of Fitness required. Alaska pay is real, but the board's thin.

**LU-26 Washington, DC** shows 60 calls against 461 hands—massive overage—but data center build-out is pulling talent harder than the board depth suggests; JE Richards and Freestate competing for same Ashburn/Sterling infrastructure work.

Data centers are still the gravitational center; Milwaukee and Salt Lake are the cleanest paths right now.

LINEMAN.text:
**Trampin the IBEW Lineman Locals — Saturday, September 5, 2026**

**LU-71 Columbus, OH** is a churn machine right now — 46 calls, 140 hands needed. NEW RIVER ELECT. CORP. is running two separate distro pushes: 40 JL's on 10-hour days (nights stayed plus **$125 bonus** daily, PD **$125**) and 9 more JL's on 4-10s with optional weekend stretches. Both need CDL. This is volume work, not premium pay, but steady if you can stack hours.

**LU-84 Newnan, GA** is tighter — 32 calls, 105 hands — but SERVICE ELECTRIC is stacking work. The Social Circle energize job for GA Power runs **$46.8** and **$56.8** depending on the call (barehand cert required on the higher one). Statewide substation tech work at **$44.46**. PD runs **$100–$150/day**. Grid and barehand experience moving the needle here.

**LU-66 Houston, TX** shows 23 calls across NHPL and Front Line. No posted scale on the board, but transmission work to Floresville gets **$175** PD and Class A CDL required. That's a pull if you're chasing out-of-area per diem in Texas heat.

**LU-1249 Cicero, NY** has 31 calls with solid depth. O'Connell's Barker job runs **$125/day** PD, JL's need CDL A and current certs. J W Didado in Ithaca goes **$150/day** PD. Upstate distro and transmission, moderate pay but steady contractor work.

**LU-1393 Indianapolis, IN** is lean at 32 calls, 50 hands, but the money shows: MJ Electric's Winamac transmission 345kv circuit pays **$67.18** with **$105/day** PD. ARC American's 12.5k rebuild in Wanatah sits at **$64.66**. Transmission certifications and experience are the gate.

**LU-70 Forestville, MD** is small — 9 calls, 15 hands — but Didado's Old Field, WV transmission work (climb required) hits **$126/hr** with **$150** PD. High-value specialty climbing is concentrated on tighter boards.

Data center and transmission work is absorbing the hands right now. Specialty certs — barehand, climb, 345kv termination — are the wage drivers across the board.

UA.text:
**Trampin the UA Locals — Saturday, September 5, 2026**

**LU-290 Portland, OR** is the board to watch this week—23 calls spread across Intel's Ronler Acres fab in Hillsboro. Apollo Mechanical's hunting CAD/BIM detailers (Ticket #71649) alongside Charter's fitter and orbital welder slots on the same tool-install phase. This is semiconductor fab work: high-purity systems, precision tooling, real craft. Book depth is tight at ~47 hands against 23 openings. If you run CAD or have orbital experience, this board moves fast.

**LU-140 Salt Lake City, UT** sits at 18 calls with 61 hands—still favorable ratio. BCS Mechanical dominates the Sego Project in West Valley (15 pipefitter journeys, 13 plumber journeys, 5 apprentice slots) on 4-10s starting Aug 3 with OT. DSI's Eagle Mountain QTS data center is running 5-8s plus rotating 5-10s and Saturdays (**$10.00**). Salt Lake's got industrial scale work and commercial data-center builds running parallel—solid depth.

**LU-213 St John, NB** shows 10 calls, ~110 hands chasing them—softer ratio but real tonnage. Stuart Olson and Irving Oil Refinery shutdown work (54 journeyman pipefitter slots, 10 apprentice) is the spine here, day-shift under NMA Agreement. B&W's fab shop adds 12 more. This is refinery turnaround work—reliable, organized, steady schedule.

**LU-325 Fredericton, NB** sits thin at 5 calls but concentrated: Irving Oil shutdown at Lorneville (40 + 33 journeyman calls working 6-10s) is a shutdown sprint. Travel and PD included. Book depth is 89 hands—these jobs will fill.

**LU-208 Denver, CO** has 12 calls for 56 hands. Kiewit's project work ($65 PD, industrial scale, 5/9s + Saturday 8) and Apollo's DC2 data center in Aurora (commercial rate + incentive) keep the board solid. US Eng. Metalworks shop work fills benches.

Refinery shutdowns and semiconductor fabs are pulling hands—seasonal turnarounds and fab expansion are the market's two engines right now.
